clue.text: One place to buy two pianos?

definitions.text: One place to buy two pianos?

parts.words: One place to buy two pianos?
parts.note: a mall is somewhere to buy things, and the middle of the word for that activity of buying is PP, two piano marks

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders where they could pick up a pair of pianos.
explanation.walkthrough: In music P stands for piano (softly). The middle two letters of SHOPPING are PP, so the centre of 'shopping' holds two pianos.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall is indeed one place to buy things, and the pun on the middle letters supplies the twist.

clue.text: Organ spotted outside public library

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for spotted wraps round the library abbreviation

parts.note: spotted means seen

explanation.surface: Someone notices a body part lying outside the local library.
explanation.definitionFit: The spleen is an abdominal organ that filters blood.

clue.text: Openly gay array of food unfolded?

parts.note: someone openly gay is out
a spread is a lavish array of food laid out

explanation.surface: A colourful, flamboyant buffet laid out for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outspread has been opened out wide, i.e. unfolded; the question mark flags the loose sense.

clue.text: Benevolent approach? Hint, and I'll come round

indicators.note: to come round is to turn about, so the letters of the preceding words are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A kindly approach: drop a hint and the other person will come round to your view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link joining the last fodder word; the fifteen letters of APPROACH, HINT and ILL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Philanthropical describes charitable goodwill towards others, a synonym of benevolent.

clue.text: Logic circuit in organ, switching bottom to top note

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom letter of the word is shifted up to the top

parts.note: taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An electronic component inside an organ, rearranged to fix a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching bottom to top' moves the final N of ORGAN to the front, giving NORGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A NOR gate is a basic digital logic element giving true only when both inputs are false.

clue.text: See 1
There must be a charge for this flower

definitions.text: There must be a charge for this flower

parts.words: There must be a charge for this flower
parts.note: the flower is something that flows, and electricity flows only when there is a charge

explanation.surface: A florist insists on payment for a particular bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as 'thing that flows', and 'charge' as electric charge rather than a price.
explanation.definitionFit: A current flows, so it is literally a flower, and an electric one is a flow of charge.

clue.text: One attempting to find German city

definitions.meaning: someone who tries or has a go
An old city on the Moselle in western Germany

explanation.surface: Someone tries to track down a city in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who tries; the other is the Roman-founded city on the Moselle.

clue.text: One could get word in this side street: bit of secrecy is needed

definitions.text: One could get word in this

parts.note: an edge is a side
a way is a road or street, as in Milky Way or Broadway

indicators.note: a bit of the word secrecy is taken to be just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to slip a message in down a side street, discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is needed' is a link. The idiom is 'get a word in edgeways', squeezing a remark into someone's monologue.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of barely managing to speak is getting a word in sideways, so this is where a word could be got.

clue.text: Braved storms courageously?

definitions.note: this is an example of the word class, not a synonym, hence the question mark

indicators.note: storms suggests violent upheaval, so the letters of the first word are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone faced the storms with real bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courageously' is a defined example: it is a word of that part of speech, which the question mark signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Courageously modifies a verb and ends in -ly, so it is one example of this part of speech.

clue.text: In Nepal, a thick stick

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A traveller describes a sturdy walking stick in Nepal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick used in South Asia, often by police.

clue.text: Once again making judgment that is compensatory

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
deeming is judging or considering

explanation.surface: A retrial reaches a verdict that makes up for an earlier wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A redeeming quality makes up for faults, so it is compensating, as in 'redeeming features'.

clue.text: Flat place to walk in E Andes, winding round about mountain

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the reversed peak
a winding path twists, so the letters of the place name are twisted into a new order
about signals that the word for a mountain is turned back to front

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A walker in the eastern Andes follows a winding path round a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal but turns the mountain backwards; 'round' does the containing, inside the letters 'winding' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level promenade, typically along a seafront, made for strolling.

clue.text: It's worth changing chair cover

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the word beside it are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone decides it is worth replacing the chair's upholstery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A throw is a loose decorative cloth draped over a sofa or armchair.

clue.text: Liverpool's finest thrashed the French

parts.note: beat means thrashed, defeated heavily
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: A Liverpool football star beat the French side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles were the Liverpool band, so one member is among the city's most celebrated sons.

clue.text: Times crossword solution found in this English soldier's home?

indicators.note: found in tells us one piece is discovered sitting inside the other

parts.note: times as in multiplication is by, as in three by four
a light is a crossword answer entered in the grid

explanation.surface: A Times crossword answer turns out to be an English soldier's word for home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is multiplication. 'this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers serving abroad have long used the slang Blighty for Britain or England as home.

clue.text: Base compound partly in centre of Soho

definitions.text: Base compound partly in centre of Soho

parts.words: Base compound partly in centre of Soho
parts.note: the middle letters of Soho are O and H, which is the chemical formula of the ion that makes this alkaline compound

explanation.surface: A seedy compound partly located in central Soho, the London nightlife district.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a London district; its two central letters OH are the formula for the ion of this base, so the compound is partly there.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydroxides such as sodium hydroxide are bases, and the hydroxide ion is written OH.

clue.text: Bad egg reeked? Not good in breakfast dish

indicators.note: bad suggests spoiled, so the letters of the phrase are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rotten egg stinks out the breakfast plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not good' means the letters of EGG REEKED, minus one G, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a rice, smoked fish and egg dish, a classic of the Victorian breakfast table.

clue.text: Stop by river, at middle of tidal bore

parts.note: an end is a stop or finish
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: the middle of the word tidal is its central letter

explanation.surface: A tidal bore is halted by a river, the wave stopping midstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'at' are links. 'bore' looks like the noun (tidal bore) but is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, meaning tolerated, which is what endured means.

clue.text: Those giving number within group

indicators.note: within says the abbreviation sits inside the name of the band

parts.note: the Doors were a rock group fronted by Jim Morrison

explanation.surface: Charitable contributors counted within an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Donors are people who give money, blood or organs.

clue.text: Source of amusement, having pulled a cracker a bit back

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read backwards
a bit means only a short run of letters inside these words is wanted

explanation.surface: Christmas fun, pulling a cracker a moment ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link; the letters EDACRA sit across 'pulled a cracker' and read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade, full of slot machines and games, is a place of entertainment.

clue.text: Counsel one son in 9, endlessly

indicators.note: in says the two letters go into the shortened word
endlessly removes the final letter of the answer to the referenced clue

parts.note: the answer to 9 down
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lawyer advises a son, cross-referencing another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from ADVERB, leaving ADVER, and IS goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel can mean a legal or other consultant who gives guidance, a person who advises.

clue.text: Model fixed up for formal ball?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sit is to model, as for a portrait
set means fixed, as in set in place

explanation.surface: A model is fixed up with a date for a formal dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for formal' is read: the answer is the formal word for a ball, a testicle. 'ball' looks like a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball is slang for testicle, and testis is the formal anatomical term for it.

clue.text: Get a little grapefruit

indicators.note: a little of the word means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: a rasp is a short informal name for a raspberry

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy a small grapefruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grapefruit' is split in two: 'a little' applies to 'grape' alone, and 'fruit' is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an idea is to understand it, which is to grasp it.

clue.text: Passage from Mordecai's letter

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A passage taken from a letter written by Mordecai.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage.

clue.text: Woman meeting Romeo or me, possibly all afternoon? Not even once again

indicators.note: all after means every other piece comes after the noon letter

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name, the first woman in Genesis
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: possibly signals that the two short words may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A woman spends the whole afternoon with Romeo or the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afternoon' is split as 'after noon': everything else follows N for noon. 'meeting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, famous from Poe's raven, means never again, not on one further occasion.

clue.text: Health treatments doing no good then?

definitions.text: Health treatments doing no good then?

parts.words: Health treatments doing no good then?
parts.note: read as 'the others cure', implying these particular treatments do not

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether some therapies are useless.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase splits as 'the rest cure', i.e. the remaining ones heal, so these do no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a regime of bed rest prescribed for nervous or physical illness.

clue.text: Be discriminatory? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially means drop the first letter

parts.note: sexist means discriminating on grounds of gender

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are being prejudiced, at least not at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is to live or have reality, a synonym of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Duo very sober, with the drunk holding hands

indicators.note: holding means the shuffled letters hold the two hand abbreviations
a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two hands

explanation.surface: A sober pair and a drunk companion walk along holding hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'drunk' rearranges VERY SOBER THE into EVE...YBROTHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Everly Brothers were an American singing pair famed for close harmony.
